Comment: M7 extraction pipeline (D-035, docs/architecture/reviews/m7-extraction-design/claude-reconciliation-final-design.md, GATE 9.2/9.3). RunTextract/RunDeterministicParser/RunBedrock/ValidateSchema/CompareExtractors/PersistExtractedFields/MarkPendingConfirmation/CompleteRun are all real Task states (items 4-7, ExtractionValidationTaskHandler included). infra/modules/extraction-workflow/ (parameterized by Lambda ARN variables) is wired into the module.extraction_workflow resource in infra/main.tf - see NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md for current wiring/deploy status.

RunTextract.Comment: The only real Task state for this phase (design §2, rodada 5 correction: no separate DetectDocumentType state - classification happens INSIDE this single TextractTaskHandler invocation, per §1.2). Sequence inside the handler: classify -> OCR kill switch -> reserve AI_CALL quota -> StartDocumentTextDetection -> persist TextractJob, then return (no SendTaskSuccess here - the execution stays parked on taskToken until a LATER, separate SQS-triggered COMPLETE_OCR invocation resolves it via SendTaskSuccess/Failure).

Catch.Comment: UnsupportedDocumentTypeError/OcrDisabledError/TextractUnsupportedDocumentError/TextractJobPersistenceFailedError are unhandled exceptions thrown synchronously inside startOcr() (START_OCR invocation) - Step Functions surfaces these as the Lambda's errorType, i.e. the JS Error class name, never AppError.code (found in the 2026-08-27 real E2E run, NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md - the previous version of this Catch used the .code values and never matched). TextractPartialFailure is different: completeOcr() (the later, SQS-triggered COMPLETE_OCR invocation) never throws it - it constructs a TextractPartialFailureError purely to read its .code and passes that string verbatim as the `error` argument of an explicit SendTaskFailure call (sfn-task-token-sender.ts), so Step Functions sees the literal code string here, not the class name - keep this one as-is if the sender contract doesn't change.
Catch-all for any other/unclassified error (ASL requires States.ALL alone in its own ErrorEquals, separate from the named errors above) - same fallback to the deterministic parser.

RunDeterministicParser.Comment: PdfParserTaskHandler (item 5, D-035 SS1.3) - real Lambda now. Runs a deterministic parser over the OCR artifact (when present) to produce candidate field values, per implementation-blueprint.md SS12.5. A RunTextract failure above (ocrFailure present) still reaches this state and must run degraded (no OCR text, returns no candidates rather than a fabricated file-metadata heuristic - see NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md pending decision) - never skipped. Item 6 correction: ResultSelector+OutputPath now unwrap the raw arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke response (which wraps the handler's real return value under Payload/ExecutedVersion/StatusCode) down to the handler's own RunDeterministicParserOutput shape, so every state from here on (NeedsBedrock/CheckAiKillSwitch/RunBedrock) reads $.needsBedrock/$.aiExtractionEnabled/$.artifact directly - RunBedrock's own Payload.$: "$" therefore sends RunBedrockExtractionInput (mirroring RunDeterministicParserOutput exactly, see run-bedrock-extraction.ts) straight to BedrockExtractionTaskHandler, unwrapped. ValidateSchema (item 7, still a stub) will need its own OutputPath once RunBedrock's real output shape is finalized together with item 7.

Catch.Comment: The ONE failure that goes straight to MarkPendingConfirmation without trying Bedrock - a RunDeterministicParser failure itself, per design §1.2. ResultPath here means the Catch payload is NOT run through ResultSelector/OutputPath above (those only apply to a successful Task result), so $ keeps its pre-Task shape (either completeOcr's re-attached context, or the original execution input) with .parserFailure appended - the same shape MarkPendingConfirmation already expected before this state existed for real.

NeedsBedrock.Comment: Real condition (item 6) - $.needsBedrock is now a top-level field of RunDeterministicParser's unwrapped output (see that state's ResultSelector/OutputPath above).

CheckAiKillSwitch.Comment: AI_EXTRACTION kill switch gate before any paid Bedrock call, fail-closed per design §1.5 - $.aiExtractionEnabled was read once by RunDeterministicParser (AppConfig call) and is re-checked again, defense in depth, inside BedrockExtractionTaskHandler itself (run-bedrock-extraction.ts) before it spends the quota reservation.

RunBedrock.Comment: BedrockExtractionTaskHandler (item 6, D-035 SS1.9/SS1.11) - real Lambda now. Converse API, prompt isolation (versioned immutable system message, untrusted user block, closed submit_extraction tool schema with forced tool choice, temperature 0, token limit), BedrockExtractionRequest carries only textArtifact (never raw OCR text - the adapter resolves it internally via OcrArtifactStore.get()), AI_CALL quota reserved (idempotent per runId|BEDROCK, same pattern as RunTextract's runId|TEXTRACT) before the call. Input is RunDeterministicParser's unwrapped output directly (Payload.$: "$" - see that state's comment); same invoke shape as RunDeterministicParser (no waitForTaskToken), so its own output needs the identical unwrap for whatever consumes it next (item 7, not yet implemented - left as a plain lambda:invoke wrapper here since ValidateSchema is still a stub).

Catch.Comment: A RunBedrock failure never re-fabricates a value and never blocks the run - it still proceeds to ValidateSchema/CompareExtractors with only the deterministic candidates available, exactly like the ocrFailure/parserFailure Catches above degrade gracefully rather than dead-ending the execution. ResultPath here means the Catch payload is NOT run through ResultSelector/OutputPath above (those only apply to a successful Task result), so $ keeps RunDeterministicParser's already-unwrapped output (extractedFields/needsBedrock/etc. all still top-level) with .bedrockFailure appended - ValidateSchema still finds $.extractedFields where it expects it.

ValidateSchema.Comment: ExtractionValidationTaskHandler (item 7, D-035 §2, real Lambda now) - first of 5 distinct operations of the SAME Lambda (kept as separate Task states for per-stage audit/Catch, design §2's closing paragraph - overhead is negligible next to Textract/Bedrock). Marks each candidate valid/invalid against field-schema.ts's declared valueType (run-extraction-validation.ts's validateSchema()); never drops a field, only flags it. Same unwrap pattern as RunDeterministicParser/RunBedrock (ResultSelector+OutputPath) - the handler's real return value becomes $ directly for CompareExtractors.

CompareExtractors.Comment: Compares deterministic vs. Bedrock candidates per schema field (compare-extractors.ts's ExtractionAgreement: SINGLE_SOURCE/MATCH/MISMATCH) - pure, never touches DynamoDB/S3. Produces $.comparedFields for PersistExtractedFields.

PersistExtractedFields.Comment: Writes ExtractedField rows + transitions ExtractionRun to a terminal status (COMPLETED, or DISCARDED on a concurrent-discard race - design §3's TOCTOU close) in ONE TransactWriteItems (DynamoDbExtractedFieldStore.commitRunOutcome). Deliberately NEVER deletes the transient OCR artifact here - only CompleteRun (next) does, per design §3's governing invariant. A transient DynamoDB failure is retried by this state's own Retry (never routed to MarkPendingConfirmation, which is reserved for the RunDeterministicParser hard-failure branch only).

MarkPendingConfirmation.Comment: Reached ONLY from RunDeterministicParser's own hard failure (design §1.2's parserFailure Catch, above) - no ValidateSchema/CompareExtractors/PersistExtractedFields ever ran for this execution. Writes every schema field as PENDING_CONFIRMATION with no candidate, transitions ExtractionRun to FAILED (or DISCARDED on the same concurrent-discard race), AND deletes the transient OCR artifact if one exists - design §3 names this state explicitly as a deletion point ('em caminho FAILED'), since this branch never reaches CompleteRun.

CompleteRun.Comment: Terminal success state on the normal path - PersistExtractedFields already committed the DB outcome; this state's ONLY job is deleting the transient OCR artifact if one exists (design §3: 'o único ponto do sistema que sabe com certeza que nenhum estado subsequente vai mais ler o artefato' - true here because this state has no Next).
